core_obligations: Construct the two quasi-inverses: chi((A,f),b) := hfiber f b and psi(P) := (Sigma b:B, P(b), proj1) (source lines 828-833).
First round trip: for P : B -> type, the retained fiber-of-a-fibration lemma gives hfiber proj1 b ~ P(b) for every b, so P is homotopic to chi(psi(P)) (source lines 836-839).
Second round trip: for f : A -> B one must produce a path from (Sigma b:B, hfiber f b, proj1) to (A,f) (source lines 840-843).

Use the retained identification of the total space of the fibers with A to get an equivalence e with e(b,a,p) = a and e^{-1}(a) = (f(a),a,refl), and reduce by the sigma-path characterisation to showing trans (ua(e)) proj1 = f (source lines 844-847).

Compute that transport by the univalence computation rule together with the retained transport-arrow identity to get proj1 o e^{-1}, which is definitionally f by the definition of e^{-1} (source line 848).

proof_roadmap.step: Write down the two candidate quasi-inverses.

Second round trip via the retained total-space identification, the sigma-path characterisation and the univalence computation rule.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 4.8.3 at source lines 821-826: for any type B the map chi sending a pair (A,f) and a point b to the fiber of f at b is an equivalence from Sigma A:type, (A -> B) to B -> type. The author's proof (source lines 827-850) is an explicit quasi-inverse construction in which the two round trips require different inputs: the first is immediate from the retained lemma computing the fiber of a projection (lines 836-839), while the second needs a path between two elements of a sigma type, which is reduced by the sigma-path characterisation to the transport equation trans (ua(e)) proj1 = f (lines 840-847) and then discharged by combining the univalence computation rule with the retained transport-arrow identity, the inverse map e^{-1} being defined precisely so that the composite is definitionally f (line 848). The statement is a single equivalence and hides that the second round trip is a transport computation along a univalence path.
